phases.name: slice-01-overflow-menu — The ⋯ menu replaces the armed ×; Delete list reaches the shipped dialog unchanged.

steps.name: Render the ⋯ trigger and the four-item menu per column in the shared board_columns
steps.description: Render the ⋯ trigger and the four-item menu per column in the shared board_columns.html partial, remove the [data-lane-delete] × , and carry the four action URLs on BoardColumn.
criteria: Every rendered column carries exactly one button[data-action=toggle-lane-menu][data-lane={slug}].
No [data-lane-delete] marker appears anywhere in either render path.
The menu container [data-lane-menu={slug}] holds Edit list, Insert list before, Insert list after, Delete list in that order.
Action URLs are built in views::board_columns from validated path slugs, never slugify(name).
Scenarios green: 'The column header offers a menu, not an armed delete', 'The menu lists exactly the four lane operations'.
scenario_name: The column header offers a menu, not an armed delete
The menu lists exactly the four lane operations
steps.implementation_notes: Render the ⋯ trigger and the four-item menu per column in the shared board_columns.html partial, remove the [data-lane-delete] × , and carry the four action URLs on BoardColumn.

steps.name: Add the menu as the fourth arm of keyboard
steps.description: Add the menu as the fourth arm of keyboard.js::closeTopLayer(), with DOM-derived open state, two branches on the existing delegated click listener, focus return, and menu CSS re-hashed into the stylesheet.
criteria: keyboard.js registers NO new Escape listener and NO second document click listener (BR-4).
menuIsOpen() queries the DOM; no module-level open-menu variable exists.
Escape closes the menu and returns focus to its ⋯ trigger; the board is otherwise unchanged.
One Escape peels exactly one layer with help open above a menu.
A menu open across an out-of-band #board-columns refresh does not leave Escape a silent no-op.
Stylesheet re-hashed and static/VENDOR.md row updated in the same change; check-arch R2/R3 pass.
Browser scenarios green: Delete-list-reaches-dialog, Escape-closes-and-returns-focus, keyboard-operable, menu-survives-OOB, Escape-peels-one-layer.
scenario_name: Delete list reaches the shipped dialog unchanged
Escape closes the menu and returns focus, changing nothing
The menu is reachable and operable without a pointer
The menu survives the board refreshing underneath it
Escape peels one layer at a time with a menu open
steps.implementation_notes: Add the menu as the fourth arm of keyboard.js::closeTopLayer(), with DOM-derived open state, two branches on the existing delegated click listener, focus return, and menu CSS re-hashed into the stylesheet.

Both re-premised scenarios are green in the browser lane.

The delete dialog closes like every other dialog, leaving the board alone
steps.implementation_notes: Re-premise the two shipped board-lane-management browser scenarios that click button[data-lane-delete] directly so they open the menu first.

phases.name: slice-02-edit-lane — Edit list renames a lane's label and touches nothing else.

steps.name: Implement the lane-name validation seam plus Store::rename_lane and the services rename use case, replacing the DISTILL
steps.description: Implement the lane-name validation seam plus Store::rename_lane and the services rename use case, replacing the DISTILL scaffolds.
criteria: One validation seam serves rename and (later) insert: trimmed non-blank, <= 64 chars, enforced below the adapter rather than only by the DB CHECK.
Store::rename_lane updates label only; slug, position and every issues.state are provably unchanged.
Absent lane / non-member / signed-out resolve to NotFound.
Unit tests cover the validation seam boundaries (0, 1, 64, 65 chars, whitespace-only).
steps.implementation_notes: Implement the lane-name validation seam plus Store::rename_lane and the services rename use case, replacing the DISTILL scaffolds.

steps.name: Wire the edit dialog GET and rename confirm POST handlers plus the edit-lane modal template, replacing the 501 scaffolds
steps.description: Wire the edit dialog GET and rename confirm POST handlers plus the edit-lane modal template, replacing the 501 scaffolds.
criteria: GET renders the dialog pre-filled with the lane's current label, carrying _csrf and data-action=close-modal.
POST success answers the OOB #board-columns refresh; validation failure is a 422 fragment into [data-error-slot].
Non-member GET and POST are both byte-identical to a never-existed path.
Duplicate labels are permitted; only slugs are unique.
All six US-BLO-02 scenarios green.
scenario_name: Renaming a lane changes the header and nothing else
A rename never touches lane identity
The edit dialog opens showing the lane's current name
An empty or over-long lane name is refused inline
A rename is refused without the board's token and accepted with it
Two lanes may carry the same label because labels are not identity
steps.implementation_notes: Wire the edit dialog GET and rename confirm POST handlers plus the edit-lane modal template, replacing the 501 scaffolds.

phases.name: slice-03-insert-lane — Insert list before/after places a working lane exactly where asked, under one locked transaction.

steps.name: Implement foundry_core::lane_slug with unit and property tests
steps.description: Implement foundry_core::lane_slug with unit and property tests.
criteria: Underscore separator, letter-anchored, lane_ prefix on a digit-leading result, empty on no usable characters.
Table tests cover Staging, In Progress, Code Review!!, 2024 Review, ..., blank.
Property: output is a fixed point, and always either satisfies ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ or is empty.
lane_slug lives in foundry-core; check-arch single-slugify rule still passes.
steps.implementation_notes: Implement foundry_core::lane_slug with unit and property tests.

steps.name: Implement Store::insert_lane_at as one locked transaction: FOR UPDATE, anchor by identity, capture position before the s
steps.description: Implement Store::insert_lane_at as one locked transaction: FOR UPDATE, anchor by identity, capture position before the shift, slug pre-check, plain UPDATE shift, insert.
criteria: No SET CONSTRAINTS call and no new migration; the counter stays at 0015.
Concurrent inserts at one anchor both commit; neither surfaces a raw duplicate-key error.
Positions stay contiguous from zero and unique after every insert.
Zero issue rows and zero change events written.
Store-level integration test covers the concurrent case.
scenario_name: Two operators inserting at the same anchor both land
steps.implementation_notes: Implement Store::insert_lane_at as one locked transaction: FOR UPDATE, anchor by identity, capture position before the shift, slug pre-check, plain UPDATE shift, insert.

steps.name: Wire the insert services use case, the two insert handlers, and the insert dialog template
steps.description: Wire the insert services use case, the two insert handlers, and the insert dialog template.
criteria: Unrecognised {side} answers the uniform non-enumerable 404, never a 400.
Slug collision is a 422 naming the conflict; empty normalisation is a 422 asking for letters or numbers.
An inserted lane is immediately first-class on board render, dnd, edit-dialog options and /api/v1 validation.
All nine US-BLO-03 scenarios green, including the concurrency scenario.
scenario_name: Inserting before a lane places the new lane immediately to its left
Inserting after the last lane appends at the far right
An inserted lane is a fully working lane immediately
A name whose slug collides with an existing lane is refused inline
A name with no usable characters is refused inline
A lane name that cannot start a slug still becomes a working lane
An unrecognised insert side is indistinguishable from an unknown lane
A non-member cannot insert a lane
A non-member reaching the lane routes gets the uniform not-found
steps.implementation_notes: Wire the insert services use case, the two insert handlers, and the insert dialog template.
